name: Fading Affect Bias
description: The emotional sting of negative autobiographical memories tends to fade faster over time than the positive feeling attached to good memories. As time passes, the remembered emotional balance of the past can drift upward.
design_relevance_note: Thin but real relevance to delayed feedback, long-gap satisfaction studies, churn interviews, and remembered-experience research: users may not remember bad feelings with the same intensity they originally had. It matters more to interpretation of retrospective data than to everyday interface pattern decisions.
prevalence_note: A stable academic term in autobiographical-memory research, but uncommon in mainstream product-design vocabulary outside specialized UX research interpretation.

findings.description: Reviewing fading-affect-bias research, Walker and Skowronski conclude that affect associated with negative autobiographical memories fades faster than affect associated with positive memories, and that this pattern has been observed across multiple methods and populations.
findings.source_title: The Fading affect bias: But what the hell is it for?
